transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Novapay Head of ML), Tom Keller (Novapay Infra), Priya Rao (Novapay SRE)

Summary: quick recap of last week's run, observed queueing at ~150-170 concurrent requests, p99 spikes. Discussed continuous batching tweaks and concurrency targets.

[00:00:00] Samir: okay, welcome everyone, thanks for joining, quick check in on the POC throughput run from last night, Nina will walk through the benchmark output, then we'll go into tuning suggestions, and set next steps
[00:00:18] Nina: yeah hi all, so I pulled the runs into the bench sheet i shared, link in the chat — bench:bit.ly/novapay-throughput-0422, um so baseline run had 100 concurrent, batch target 16, avg token rate looked fine, p95 around 110ms, p99 320ms
[00:00:42] Tom: yeah and when we pushed to 160 concurrent we started seeing timeouts and queue growth, CPU on the host looked okay but GPU utilization dropped, which was surprising
[00:00:58] Nina: right, that was my note too — looks like small requests cause lots of small KV cache misses, and we end up with lots of tiny batches that aren't filling. continuous batching can help but we need to tune max latency and queue limit
[00:01:18] Maya: can you explain continuous batching again? we read the doc but the behavior under burst wasn't clear
[00:01:26] Nina: sure — continuous batching keeps an in-memory request queue per worker and will emit a batch when either the batch hits target size or a max wait time expires. so you get better fill rates under steady load, but under spiky traffic you may need to relax max_wait_ms to allow more time to fill batches
[00:01:50] Samir: and also there's the concurrency window effect — too many inflight requests means more context switches and smaller effective batch sizes, so sometimes targeting a slightly lower concurrency with higher batch target yields better throughput/cost
[00:02:06] Priya: in our run we had batch_target=16 and max_wait_ms=20, maybe that's too tight for our traffic profile with many small queries
[00:02:16] Nina: yeah, try bumping max_wait_ms to 50-80, and increase batch_target to 24-32, also set queue_limit to something like 512 to avoid backpressure shredding the pipeline
[00:02:30] Tom: what about the kv cache — our requests have a lot of prefix repetition, is that something Redwood's runtime can exploit?
[00:02:38] Nina: definitely — we have prefix/KV caching but sometimes the traces show keys aren't matching because tokenization differences or whitespace. we'll share a helper to normalize prefixes; also you can enable aggressive KV reuse which increases memory but reduces compute
[00:02:54] Maya: memory tradeoffs okay with infra, but we need to keep tail latency < 350ms p99 for user flows, p95 < 120ms ideally
[00:03:06] Samir: noted — our target for the stress run should be p95 < 120 and p99 < 350 while sustaining target rps, we'll test at different concurrency points to find sweet spot
[00:03:18] Nina: another knob is the queueing strategy — FIFO vs priority for small/large requests; for Novapay we'd want priority for low-token, high-qps merchant lookups so they don't get starved by large backfill jobs
[00:03:36] Tom: we did see a competing backfill at 03:00 that probably skewed the run, i'll make sure that doesn't run during the next stress test
[00:03:44] Maya: question on autoscaler — we saw long scale-up times, is that because boot time or because of queue drain settings?
[00:03:52] Nina: both; instance boot + model warmup adds 30-60s depending on gpu type. we can pre-warm by keeping a small buffer of idle workers, and tune scale-in/scale-out thresholds to be more aggressive on scale-out. For Dedicated you can use burst capacity for immediate headroom
[00:04:12] Samir: and remember we have model variants — a slightly quantized variant can drop cost and lower latency; we can fallback on spike events if needed
[00:04:20] Priya: any concerns about output quality with quantized variants? we don't want regressions for payment descriptions
[00:04:28] Nina: we'll run evals and diff outputs on a held-out prompt set — i'll attach the eval results side-by-side in the bench sheet so you can inspect quality delta
[00:04:40] Tom: for the stress test configuration, what are the exact parameters you recommend?
[00:04:46] Nina: recommended starting point: concurrency target 200, batch_target 32, max_wait_ms 60, queue_limit 512, timeout_ms 1200, enable kv_aggressive=true; run for 2 hours with a 5 min ramp and 5 min cool-down
[00:05:02] Samir: we'll also run a variant at concurrency 120 with batch_target 48 to compare cost per token and latency curves
[00:05:10] Maya: how should we capture traces so you can analyze micro latency sources?
[00:05:14] Priya: i can add the trace span headers and sample the p99 tails and JSON logs, is there a specific format?
[00:05:20] Nina: JSON log with timestamps and token counts is fine, include request id and model variant name, and mark whether kv cache hit. we'll provide an example snippet in the sheet
[00:05:32] Samir: quick note — there's some transcriber noise in earlier runs where "KV cache" got logged as "K V cash" in our csv, so ignore that column name if you see weird tokens
[00:05:44] Tom: ha, okay noted
[00:05:48] Maya: any blockers from Redwood side to run the stress test?
[00:05:52] Samir: none — we just need the window and you'll need to pause background jobs, also grant Nina read access to the bench sheet and the request traces location
[00:06:02] Nina: i'll upload the config snippets after the call, and share the bench sheet with edit rights
[00:06:08] Priya: budget question — if we run the 2-hr test at 200 concurrency with fallback variants, whats the expected incremental cost?
[00:06:16] Samir: rough estimate in the sheet, depends on model variant; for your committed Dedicated pool we can apply a discount, we'll include a cost-of-test calc in the bench sheet line items
[00:06:28] Maya: can we automate alerting on p99 regression during the test so we can kill early?
[00:06:34] Nina: yes, set an automatic abort if p99 > 450ms for more than 2 consecutive 1-minute windows — we'll include an abort hook in the stress harness
[00:06:46] Tom: any thoughts on request shaping at the client level to avoid long queues? token batching client side maybe?
[00:06:52] Nina: client-side aggregation is helpful for many small requests, but it adds latency to single requests. for merchant lookups you could batch similar requests within 50-100ms window to increase server batch fill
[00:07:06] Maya: ok i think we have a plan, when will you share the bench link and config?
[00:07:10] Nina: i'll share in the next 24 hours, expected by 04/23 EOD
[00:07:16] Samir: recap of next steps, run date target 04/28, Nina posts configs and bench sheet, Priya uploads traces, Maya confirms success criteria — anything else?
[00:07:28] Priya: i'll also add a list of production traffic patterns so you can simulate realistic bursts
[00:07:32] Tom: i'll disable the backfill during the run window
[00:07:36] Maya: thanks everyone, good sync
[00:07:38] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up via sheet and calendar invite for the run, bye

Post-call notes: SE attached config snippet and bench link. Action items reflected above. Some transcription artifacts ("K V cash") present in previous CSV export.
